title: Texas City: When a Burning Cargo Became a Harbor Disaster
dek: The 1947 explosions at Texas City connect hazardous cargo, waterfront industry and emergency response across one port system.
event: In April 1947, a fire aboard the Grandcamp in Texas City preceded an ammonium-nitrate explosion that devastated the waterfront and was followed by another ship explosion. This draft asks how cargo handling, fire response and nearby industrial facilities turned an emergency aboard one vessel into a city-scale catastrophe.
mechanism: The record must distinguish the initial cargo fire, the first explosion, secondary industrial damage and the later High Flyer explosion. It must also separate contemporary descriptions of smoke and firefighting from later explanations of ammonium nitrate behavior.
system: The central systems question is how a port governs incompatible risks when ships, warehouses, refineries, rail lines and residential districts share the same geography.
memory: Texas City is frequently remembered through a single blast image, which can hide the sequence between the first warning, evacuation choices, cascading damage and the second vessel.

title: Feyzin: The Refinery Fire That Changed the Language of LPG Risk
dek: A leaking storage sphere, road traffic and emergency operations converged at Feyzin in 1966.
event: The 1966 disaster at the Feyzin refinery near Lyon began with a release of liquefied petroleum gas and escalated through fire and vessel failure. The episode became a reference point for understanding boiling-liquid expanding-vapor explosions, but the technical label should not replace the event sequence.
mechanism: A finished account must reconstruct the release, ignition, heat exposure and failure of pressurized storage without treating every later LPG accident as identical. The positions of responders, road users and equipment are essential to the chronology.
system: Feyzin raises questions about facility siting, traffic control, isolation systems and whether emergency plans recognized that responders themselves could be placed inside the escalation zone.
memory: The acronym BLEVE often carries the story, while the organizational decisions that allowed a local release to threaten multiple vessels receive less attention.

title: San Juanico: A Storage Terminal and the Geography of Escalation
dek: The 1984 LPG disaster outside Mexico City exposed how storage layout and nearby settlement can compound one another.
event: In November 1984, a release and fire at the San Juan Ixhuatepec LPG terminal developed into multiple explosions near densely populated neighborhoods. The article focuses on escalation across a storage site and the boundary between an industrial facility and the community around it.
mechanism: The reporting must identify which tanks and pipes were involved, how the initial release was detected, how fire spread and which later explosions are supported by investigation rather than eyewitness shorthand.
system: The event tests land-use controls, emergency warning, terminal layout and the assumption that a facility boundary is also a risk boundary.
memory: Photographs of fireballs dominate later accounts, while displacement, identification of victims and the long administrative aftermath are harder to recover.

title: Pasadena 1989: Isolation, Maintenance and a Vapor Cloud
dek: The Phillips explosion in Pasadena turned maintenance isolation into a plant-wide test of safeguards.
event: An explosion and fire at the Phillips Petroleum complex in Pasadena, Texas, in October 1989 followed a release of flammable process material during maintenance work. This draft examines how isolation practices, operating authority and emergency response interacted.
mechanism: The technical account must trace the maintenance configuration, valve or line status, release formation, ignition and subsequent fires using investigation records rather than generalized accounts of a refinery blast.
system: The institutional question is whether maintenance work was treated as an exception outside normal process control or as a high-risk operating state requiring equivalent discipline and verification.
memory: Later process-safety regulation can make the earlier plant seem obviously deficient, but the article must show which practices were actually known, required and contested at the time.

title: BP Texas City: The Startup That Reached Beyond the Blowdown Drum
dek: The 2005 refinery explosion linked startup operations, temporary offices and company-level cost and safety decisions.
event: During startup of an isomerization unit at BP's Texas City refinery in March 2005, hydrocarbons overflowed into a blowdown system, formed a vapor cloud and exploded. The draft follows the event from control-room indications to the location of occupied trailers.
mechanism: The record must distinguish immediate equipment and operating failures from the broader findings about alarm performance, instrumentation, procedures, supervision and siting.
system: This is a case about the distance between personal-safety metrics and process-safety risk, and about whether corporate oversight could see deteriorating barriers before a catastrophic startup.
memory: The phrase cost cutting is often used as a complete explanation; the article should instead map the specific decisions, warnings and deferred improvements that investigators documented.

source.title: CSB BP America refinery explosion final report

title: Buncefield: The Tank That Kept Filling
dek: At Buncefield, failed level protection allowed a fuel transfer to become a vast vapor-cloud explosion.
event: In December 2005, petrol overflowed from a storage tank at the Buncefield oil depot in Hertfordshire, producing a vapor cloud that ignited and damaged a wide area. The article treats the event as a chain of measurement, shutdown and containment failures.
mechanism: The chronology needs to follow the incoming transfer, gauge behavior, independent high-level protection, overflow, vapor movement and ignition without collapsing them into one equipment fault.
system: Buncefield asks how independent a safety layer is when its testing, maintenance or assumptions remain connected to the same operating organization.
memory: The size of the blast is memorable; the quieter preconditions inside level measurement and proof testing are less visible but more transferable.

title: T2 Laboratories: When Scale-Up Outran Cooling
dek: A runaway reaction in Jacksonville made process scale-up and relief design matters of public record.
event: A reactor exploded at T2 Laboratories in Jacksonville, Florida, in December 2007 during production of a gasoline additive. The draft centers on heat generation, cooling capacity and what changed as a process moved beyond laboratory scale.
mechanism: The account must explain reaction acceleration and pressure development without implying that a single temperature reading tells the whole story. Relief design, cooling reliability and available hazard testing require separate treatment.
system: The broader question is how a smaller company obtains, interprets and acts on reactive-hazard knowledge when scaling a process and designing emergency protection.
memory: Runaway reaction is a useful technical description, but it can obscure the prior design choices that determined whether runaway conditions were anticipated and survivable.

title: Imperial Sugar: The Dust Hazard Hidden in Routine Production
dek: The 2008 explosion at Port Wentworth showed how combustible dust can accumulate inside ordinary material-handling systems.
event: An explosion and fire at the Imperial Sugar refinery in Port Wentworth, Georgia, in February 2008 spread through areas where sugar dust had accumulated. This article asks how a familiar product became fuel across connected spaces.
mechanism: The draft must distinguish the suspected initiating event from the secondary explosions that propagated through dust layers and enclosed handling equipment. Housekeeping, enclosure changes and ventilation need dated evidence.
system: Imperial Sugar tests whether hazards outside a company's main product narrative receive the same engineering attention as the production process itself.
memory: Sugar appears benign in daily life, which makes the hazard easy to tell as a surprise; the record instead points toward known combustible-dust behavior and preventable accumulation.

title: West Fertilizer: Storage, Fire and the Distance to the Community
dek: The 2013 explosion in West, Texas, made inventory, responder information and land-use separation part of one inquiry.
event: A fire at the West Fertilizer Company facility in April 2013 preceded an explosion that damaged nearby homes, schools and care facilities. The draft examines hazardous inventory, firefighter information and community proximity.
mechanism: The article must separate what investigators established about ammonium nitrate storage and fire exposure from disputed or unresolved questions about how the fire began.
system: The systems issue is fragmented authority: fire codes, environmental reporting, workplace regulation, local planning and emergency response can each hold part of the risk without owning the whole.
memory: Accounts often seek one regulatory gap, but the geography of the damage shows how several ordinary permissions can combine into exceptional exposure.

title: Philadelphia Energy Solutions: A Refinery Fire and an Aging System
dek: The 2019 Philadelphia refinery explosion exposed the consequences of a hydrofluoric-acid release and long-lived equipment.
event: A fire and explosions at the Philadelphia Energy Solutions refinery in June 2019 followed a process release in the alkylation unit. This draft connects equipment condition, hazardous chemistry and the refinery's place inside a city.
mechanism: The technical narrative must trace the failed component, the release, ignition, vessel damage and hydrofluoric-acid safeguards using the final investigation rather than dramatic video alone.
system: The case asks how aging infrastructure, inspection programs and ownership changes affect the reliability of safety-critical equipment over decades.
memory: The spectacular fireball became the visual record, while corrosion mechanisms, inspection intervals and the facility's economic history are harder to see.

source.title: CSB Philadelphia Energy Solutions final report

title: Courrières: Rescue, Survival and the Politics of a Mine Disaster
dek: The 1906 Courrières explosion became a crisis of rescue, labor and public trust across northern France.
event: An explosion swept through the Courrières coalfield in northern France in March 1906. The scale of death, the disputed rescue effort and the later emergence of survivors made the catastrophe both an industrial and political event.
mechanism: The draft must reconstruct fire reports, ventilation changes, the explosion and access to damaged workings while distinguishing contemporary testimony from later legend.
system: Courrières asks who controls rescue decisions when the operator, engineers, state officials, workers and families have different information and different authority.
memory: The story of survivors returning after weeks underground can eclipse the arguments over rescue termination, labor protest and the names of those who did not return.

title: Senghenydd: The Explosion Behind Britain's Worst Mining Loss
dek: The 1913 Universal Colliery explosion tested ventilation, dust control and accountability in the South Wales coalfield.
event: An explosion at the Universal Colliery at Senghenydd in October 1913 killed hundreds of miners and rescuers. This draft follows the physical disaster alongside the inspection and legal systems that preceded it.
mechanism: The reporting must separate ignition evidence from the propagation role attributed to coal dust and must use the inquiry record before assigning responsibility for ventilation or electrical conditions.
system: The institutional focus is whether penalties, inspections and ownership structures created incentives proportionate to catastrophic underground risk.
memory: National superlatives preserve the scale but can flatten a workforce into a number and detach the disaster from prior warnings and later compensation.

title: Benxihu: Occupation, Coal and the Record of a Mine Catastrophe
dek: The 1942 Benxihu disaster sits inside the history of Japanese occupation, forced labor and incomplete records.
event: An explosion at the Benxihu colliery in occupied Manchuria in April 1942 caused an enormous loss of life. The event cannot be separated from wartime labor conditions, colonial control and the limits of the surviving record.
mechanism: The article must verify accounts of the explosion, ventilation response, sealed workings and recovery operations against records produced under occupation and later historical research.
system: Benxihu raises the question of how safety, labor coercion and information control interact when workers cannot freely refuse dangerous conditions or challenge the official account.
memory: The disaster is often ranked by casualty count, yet the reliability of the count and the identities and status of workers require more scrutiny than the ranking itself.

title: Farmington No. 9: The Explosion That Reshaped Federal Mine Law
dek: The 1968 Farmington mine disaster linked an inaccessible underground scene to a national legislative response.
event: Explosions and fire struck the Consol No. 9 mine near Farmington, West Virginia, in November 1968. Rescue efforts failed to reach many miners, and the mine was sealed while questions about methane, ventilation and oversight remained.
mechanism: Because investigators could not immediately inspect every part of the mine, the article must distinguish physical evidence from inference and later reopening work.
system: The policy question is how catastrophe changes federal authority: what the 1969 mine-safety law required, what Farmington directly influenced and what came from the wider record of coal deaths.
memory: The law that followed is easier to summarize than the evidentiary limits created by a burning, sealed mine and the families left without recoveries.

title: Sunshine Mine: Smoke, Self-Rescue and the Route Out
dek: The 1972 fire in Idaho turned evacuation equipment and underground communication into life-or-death infrastructure.
event: A fire in the Sunshine silver mine in Idaho in May 1972 filled underground workings with smoke and toxic gases. The draft examines warning, evacuation routes, breathing protection and the long wait for two surviving miners.
mechanism: The chronology must establish where the fire developed, how smoke traveled, what workers were told and which escape routes and respirators were available at different locations.
system: The systems question is whether emergency equipment and training were designed for the actual distance, atmosphere and confusion workers would face rather than for a nominal escape scenario.
memory: The survival of two miners after days underground is compelling, but it should not eclipse the evacuation barriers experienced by the larger workforce.

title: Upper Big Branch: Production Pressure and the Coal-Dust Chain
dek: The 2010 explosion became an investigation of ventilation, dust control, enforcement and management conduct.
event: An explosion at the Upper Big Branch mine in West Virginia in April 2010 killed miners across a large underground area. Multiple investigations examined methane ignition, coal-dust propagation, ventilation and management practices.
mechanism: The article must compare the findings and terminology of federal, state and independent investigations, noting where they converge and where legal proceedings use a different standard.
system: Upper Big Branch tests whether inspection citations, internal warnings and production decisions formed a signal strong enough to trigger intervention before catastrophe.
memory: A single ignition point is easier to narrate than the maintained conditions that allowed an explosion to travel through the mine.

source.title: West Virginia Upper Big Branch investigative report

title: Buffalo Creek: A Coal-Waste Dam and the Meaning of Natural Disaster
dek: The 1972 flood in West Virginia began with the failure of coal-waste impoundments above a populated valley.
event: In February 1972, a coal-waste impoundment failed above Buffalo Creek in West Virginia, sending water and debris through communities downstream. The event became a dispute over engineering responsibility and the language used to describe preventable harm.
mechanism: The record must reconstruct the sequence among multiple impoundments, rainfall, inspection observations and the final breach without turning a complex structure into one anonymous dam.
system: The article asks how company-built waste structures were classified, inspected and communicated to people living below them, and why official disaster language mattered for accountability.
memory: The phrase act of God became part of the public argument, sometimes overshadowing the technical record and the long psychological effects documented in the valley.

title: Hawks Nest: The Tunnel, the Dust and the Workers Missing from the Count
dek: Silica exposure during tunnel construction in West Virginia produced illness whose full toll remains disputed.
event: Workers drilling the Hawks Nest Tunnel in West Virginia during the early 1930s were exposed to intense silica dust, and many developed acute silicosis. The project sits at the intersection of industrial medicine, migrant labor and incomplete death records.
mechanism: The draft must distinguish diagnosed cases, reported deaths, later estimates and the different periods over which illness appeared. Work methods and dust controls require evidence from hearings and medical records.
system: Hawks Nest asks whose illness becomes visible when a temporary workforce is dispersed and when employment, medical and burial records are controlled by different institutions.
memory: The disaster is often assigned one toll, but the unstable count is itself evidence about labor precarity and recordkeeping.

title: Westray: The Mine, the Inquiry and Organizational Responsibility
dek: The 1992 Nova Scotia mine explosion became a case about methane, coal dust and corporate accountability.
event: An explosion at the Westray coal mine in Nova Scotia in May 1992 killed the underground crew and led to a major public inquiry. The article follows both the mine conditions and the difficulty of translating organizational failure into legal responsibility.
mechanism: The reporting must use the inquiry to trace ventilation, methane, coal dust, equipment and inspection findings while keeping later criminal proceedings analytically separate.
system: Westray asks what accountability means when hazardous practices are distributed through management structures rather than confined to one act by one person.
memory: The later Westray law is frequently invoked as the lesson, but enforcement history is necessary before presenting legal reform as closure.

title: Soma: Fire, Evacuation and the Governance of a Privatized Mine
dek: The 2014 Turkish mine disaster exposed questions about fire development, self-rescue and inspection.
event: A fire at a coal mine in Soma, Turkey, in May 2014 trapped a large underground workforce. The disaster generated technical investigations, criminal cases and national arguments about labor conditions and privatization.
mechanism: The article must compare accounts of the fire's origin, smoke movement, power loss and evacuation, and it must avoid converting contested courtroom claims into settled engineering findings.
system: Soma raises questions about subcontracting, production incentives, inspection independence and whether emergency equipment matched the time needed to reach safety.
memory: Large casualty figures drive remembrance, while shift organization, worker testimony and the differences among investigations require more patient reporting.

title: St. Francis Dam: Design Authority and the Evidence Left Downstream
dek: The 1928 collapse in California transformed a water project into a question of engineering judgment and state oversight.
event: The St. Francis Dam failed in March 1928, sending a destructive flood through the Santa Clara River valley. This draft examines design changes, geologic interpretation, warning observations and the authority concentrated in one water system.
mechanism: The failure account must distinguish what was visible before collapse from mechanisms inferred through later structural and geologic analysis. Contemporary photographs, design records and inquiry testimony should anchor the sequence.
system: The central issue is how an institution reviews the judgment of a celebrated engineer when the same organization depends on his authority and project.
memory: The collapsed dam is often treated as one man's failure, which can hide the absence of independent review and the communities erased from early official counts.

title: Malpasset: A Thin-Arch Dam and the Rock Around It
dek: The 1959 French dam failure made foundation geology as important as the concrete structure itself.
event: The Malpasset Dam near Fréjus failed in December 1959 after heavy rain and rising reservoir levels. The catastrophe became a foundational case in understanding how a dam and its abutment geology behave as one system.
mechanism: The article must trace reservoir conditions, observations, drainage and the later analysis of rock joints and uplift without reducing the failure to rainfall alone.
system: Malpasset asks how design review incorporates uncertain geology and how operators act when water management, weather and incomplete instrumentation converge.
memory: The elegance of the arch-dam design can dominate retrospective accounts, while the foundation and downstream warning problem remain less visible.

title: Teton Dam: Seepage, Erosion and a Federal Project's Collapse
dek: The 1976 Teton Dam failure turned internal erosion and design review into public evidence.
event: The newly completed Teton Dam in Idaho failed during initial reservoir filling in June 1976. The breach and downstream flooding forced examination of foundation conditions, seepage control, construction and review inside a federal water agency.
mechanism: The chronology should follow observed leaks, attempts to respond, breach development and evacuation while separating eyewitness interpretation from later findings about internal erosion.
system: The case tests whether a large project can receive genuinely independent review when schedule, institutional confidence and technical specialization all favor completion.
memory: Video of the widening breach is vivid, but it can obscure the years of design decisions that made the failure possible during the first filling.

title: Kelly Barnes Dam: Rainfall, Modification and a Lost Design Record
dek: The 1977 Georgia dam failure exposed the difficulty of assessing an old structure without complete plans.
event: Kelly Barnes Dam failed above Toccoa Falls College in November 1977 after heavy rain. Investigators had to reconstruct a structure that had been built and modified over decades without a complete modern design record.
mechanism: The article must separate rainfall loading, reservoir rise, embankment geometry and possible internal erosion, while respecting the uncertainty stated in the investigation.
system: Kelly Barnes asks how ownership and regulators should evaluate legacy dams whose construction history, materials and modifications are only partly documented.
memory: The nighttime flood is the remembered moment; the missing drawings and incremental changes are the quieter institutional story.

title: Taum Sauk: A Reservoir Without a Spillway Margin
dek: The 2005 upper-reservoir failure joined instrumentation, operating practice and design philosophy.
event: The upper reservoir of the Taum Sauk pumped-storage plant in Missouri overtopped and failed in December 2005. The draft examines water-level instruments, operating limits and the consequences of a structure designed without a conventional spillway.
mechanism: The sequence must identify instrument displacement or error, pump operation, overtopping and embankment breach, using regulatory findings rather than treating overtopping as the unexplained cause.
system: Taum Sauk asks whether independent protective layers exist when normal operation and overfill prevention rely on related instruments and assumptions.
memory: The dramatic flood through a state park can eclipse the small measurement discrepancies and procedural decisions that accumulated beforehand.

source.title: Taum Sauk pumped storage plant overview

title: Quebec Bridge: When Calculated Weight Overtook the Structure
dek: The 1907 collapse showed how design assumptions and fragmented authority can survive visible deformation.
event: The Quebec Bridge collapsed during construction in August 1907 after workers and engineers had observed deformation in critical members. The disaster became a case about calculation, communication and authority in a record-setting cantilever project.
mechanism: The article must reconstruct changes in estimated dead load, observed buckling, messages among the site and design office, and the final minutes without relying on hindsight to make every warning unambiguous.
system: The systems question is who can stop work when design authority is remote, responsibilities are divided and schedule pressure continues despite unexplained physical change.
memory: Engineering histories emphasize the erroneous calculations; the delayed response to workers reporting bent members is an equally important part of the record.

title: Silver Bridge: One Eyebar and a System Without Redundancy
dek: The 1967 Ohio River bridge collapse made fracture, inspection and structural redundancy inseparable.
event: The Silver Bridge between Point Pleasant and Kanauga collapsed during evening traffic in December 1967. Investigation focused on a tiny defect in an eyebar within a suspension chain that offered little alternative load path.
mechanism: The article should explain crack initiation and growth, the limits of inspection technology and the bridge's linked-eyebar design without suggesting that finding the final fracture explains the whole system.
system: Silver Bridge asks how inspection regimes account for structures whose critical details are inaccessible and whose failure tolerance differs from later design practice.
memory: Folklore and anniversary narratives can displace the less cinematic history of aging bridges and the federal inspection program that followed.

title: Mianus River Bridge: Drainage, Bearings and a Hidden Connection
dek: The 1983 Connecticut bridge collapse exposed how water and corrosion can defeat an inaccessible support detail.
event: A suspended span of the Mianus River Bridge on Interstate 95 collapsed in June 1983. Investigators examined a pin-and-hanger assembly, corrosion and roadway drainage that directed water toward a critical connection.
mechanism: The draft must show how the connection carried load, how corrosion and displacement developed, and what inspectors could or could not observe before collapse.
system: The event tests maintenance systems that separate drainage, deck condition and structural inspection even though the physical deterioration crosses those categories.
memory: The failed pin is easy to name; the administrative division that let water repeatedly reach it is harder to visualize.

title: Schoharie Creek: Scour Beneath an Interstate Bridge
dek: The 1987 collapse in New York turned an underwater foundation problem into a national inspection issue.
event: The Interstate 90 bridge over Schoharie Creek collapsed during flooding in April 1987 after erosion undermined a pier foundation. The event made scour assessment and underwater inspection central to bridge safety.
mechanism: The account must distinguish river flow, foundation geometry, protective material, inspection history and the timing of pier movement rather than treating floodwater as a complete explanation.
system: Schoharie Creek asks how agencies manage hazards that are largely invisible from the deck and that become most dangerous precisely when inspection is hardest.
memory: A flood appears to be an external natural force, but the record concerns how a designed structure anticipated and monitored that force over time.

title: I-35W: Gusset Plates, Added Weight and the Limits of Routine Inspection
dek: The 2007 Minneapolis bridge collapse linked an original design error to decades of modification and loading.
event: The Interstate 35W bridge over the Mississippi River collapsed during evening traffic in August 2007. Investigation identified undersized gusset plates and examined construction loads, prior modifications and inspection history.
mechanism: The technical story must explain how gusset plates connect truss members, how design thickness was determined and how later dead load and temporary construction materials affected demand.
system: The case asks why routine inspections focused on condition could miss an original design-capacity error not visible as ordinary deterioration.
memory: Images of the fallen deck dominate the event, while the mismatch between inspection for damage and review of design calculations carries the broader lesson.

title: FIU Bridge: Cracking, Peer Review and the Hours Before Collapse
dek: The 2018 pedestrian bridge collapse made visible cracking and divided authority central to the record.
event: A pedestrian bridge under construction at Florida International University collapsed over an open roadway in March 2018. Engineers had discussed significant cracking and were conducting work on the structure before it fell.
mechanism: The article must use the investigation to distinguish design errors, cracking observations, post-tensioning work and the immediate failure sequence.
system: FIU raises questions about who had authority to close the road, how peer review was scoped and how alarming field evidence moved among designer, contractor, university and transportation officials.
memory: The unusual bridge form attracts attention, but the central story is how a visible warning failed to trigger a protective operational decision.

title: Tenerife: Radio Language, Fog and Two Aircraft on One Runway
dek: The 1977 collision was not one misunderstood phrase but a chain involving diversion, visibility and cockpit coordination.
event: Two Boeing 747 aircraft collided on the runway at Los Rodeos Airport in March 1977 after diversions crowded the airport and fog reduced visibility. The draft reconstructs ground movement, radio exchanges and the takeoff decision.
mechanism: The chronology must follow each aircraft's location and each transmission, noting blocked messages and differences between words spoken, heard and interpreted.
system: Tenerife asks how standardized phraseology, cockpit hierarchy, airport surface surveillance and traffic-flow decisions manage ambiguity when several safeguards degrade together.
memory: The event is often reduced to one captain's action, which can hide the diversion, congestion, weather and communication system surrounding that action.

title: Flight 901: Navigation Data, Whiteout and the Erebus Inquiry
dek: The Antarctic crash became a dispute over route changes, visual conditions and institutional candor.
event: Air New Zealand Flight 901 struck Mount Erebus during a sightseeing flight in November 1979. The accident and subsequent inquiries examined navigation coordinates, briefing, visual conditions and the airline's account of its own systems.
mechanism: The article must distinguish the programmed route, coordinate changes, crew expectations, whiteout conditions and terrain-warning context at each stage of flight.
system: Erebus asks how an organization investigates itself and what happens when technical evidence becomes entangled with allegations about disclosure and document handling.
memory: The phrase litany of lies shapes public memory in New Zealand, but the full record requires careful separation of the accident findings from later institutional judgment.

title: Saudia 163: A Successful Landing Without an Evacuation
dek: The 1980 fire near Riyadh became a study of the minutes between touchdown and opening an exit.
event: Saudia Flight 163 returned to Riyadh after a fire was reported in the aft cargo area in August 1980. The aircraft landed and stopped, but evacuation did not begin before the cabin became unsurvivable.
mechanism: The draft must reconstruct fire detection, cockpit decisions, taxi and stopping time, engine shutdown, rescue access and door opening from the investigation record.
system: The case asks how emergency procedures prioritize aircraft control, communication and immediate evacuation when a crew has landed successfully but the hazard continues to grow.
memory: The contrast between an intact aircraft and the loss aboard it encourages moral judgment; a better article maps the information and procedural constraints minute by minute.

title: Air Canada 797: The Fire That Changed Cabin Materials and Smoke Rules
dek: A hidden in-flight fire in 1983 made smoke, flashover and evacuation timing central to cabin safety.
event: Air Canada Flight 797 diverted to Cincinnati in June 1983 after smoke and fire developed near a rear lavatory. Passengers evacuated after landing, and the cabin rapidly became engulfed.
mechanism: The article must distinguish the unresolved ignition source from established findings about smoke movement, electrical systems, cabin materials, emergency descent and the post-opening flashover.
system: The event asks how certification standards respond when a survivable landing still leaves only seconds for evacuation in a smoke-filled cabin.
memory: Later rules on smoke detectors, emergency lighting and material flammability can make the regulatory path appear automatic; the article should show what evidence changed each requirement.

title: Japan Airlines 123: A Repair, Decompression and Thirty-Two Minutes
dek: The 1985 crash connected an earlier tailstrike repair to loss of flight-control systems years later.
event: Japan Airlines Flight 123 lost control after a structural failure and decompression in August 1985, remaining airborne for more than half an hour before impact. Investigation traced the failure to an improper repair after an earlier tailstrike.
mechanism: The article must explain the pressure-bulkhead repair, fatigue growth, vertical-tail damage and hydraulic-system loss while separating investigative findings from later debates over rescue timing.
system: The systems issue is how a repair is designed, approved, inspected and carried forward through years of service after the original damage leaves organizational memory.
memory: The exceptional duration of the uncontrolled flight and the existence of survivors can overshadow the quieter maintenance-document trail that began years earlier.

title: British Airtours 28M: An Engine Fire and the Geometry of Evacuation
dek: The 1985 Manchester runway fire exposed how exits, seat layout and smoke determine survival after an aborted takeoff.
event: British Airtours Flight 28M rejected takeoff at Manchester in August 1985 after an engine failure and fire. The aircraft stopped on the runway, but fire and smoke entered the cabin during evacuation.
mechanism: The account must trace the engine failure, wind direction, stopping position, exit availability, passenger flow and cabin conditions using the investigation's timing.
system: The accident asks whether certification demonstrations represent real evacuations when smoke, blocked exits, narrow passages and human congestion replace ideal test conditions.
memory: The aircraft never became airborne, which can make the event seem like a ground fire rather than a defining test of cabin survivability.

title: Aloha 243: Corrosion, Fatigue and a Fuselage Open to the Sky
dek: The 1988 decompression over Hawaii made aging-aircraft inspection a public question.
event: A large section of the upper fuselage separated from Aloha Airlines Flight 243 in April 1988 during an inter-island flight. The crew landed the aircraft despite extensive structural damage.
mechanism: The article must explain lap-joint fatigue, corrosion, pressurization cycles and inspection practices without treating aircraft age alone as the mechanism.
system: The event asks how maintenance programs adapt when an aircraft accumulates many short cycles in a corrosive environment that differs from assumptions embedded in original design and inspection.
memory: The image of an open cabin and successful landing can turn the episode into a survival story, obscuring the inspection and aging-fleet evidence.

title: United 232: Improvised Control After Total Hydraulic Loss
dek: The 1989 DC-10 accident showed both the reach and the limit of crew improvisation after an uncontained engine failure.
event: United Airlines Flight 232 lost all three hydraulic systems after an engine disk failure in July 1989. The crew used differential thrust to reach Sioux City, where the aircraft crashed during landing.
mechanism: The account must connect metallurgical findings in the fan disk to hydraulic-line damage and then distinguish limited directional control from normal flight control.
system: United 232 asks how designers evaluate supposedly independent systems when they share physical space and can be severed by one energetic failure.
memory: The cockpit teamwork is rightly remembered, but celebration of improvisation should not replace analysis of common-location vulnerability and rescue preparation.

title: Avianca 52: Holding, Fuel and the Words Used for an Emergency
dek: The 1990 crash near New York became a case about fuel management, air-traffic flow and communication across languages.
event: Avianca Flight 52 exhausted its fuel and crashed on Long Island in January 1990 after extended holding and a missed approach to Kennedy Airport. The record spans dispatch planning, weather, air-traffic control and cockpit communication.
mechanism: The chronology must calculate fuel state only from supported records and must compare the crew's words with the emergency terminology controllers expected.
system: The accident asks how traffic systems detect deteriorating fuel margins when no single controller owns the complete flight history and when urgency is expressed indirectly.
memory: One disputed word often carries the story, while the chain of holding instructions, handoffs, weather and company planning receives less attention.

title: ValuJet 592: Oxygen Generators, Contract Maintenance and Cargo Rules
dek: The 1996 Everglades crash connected mislabeled hazardous components to a fast-growing cargo fire.
event: ValuJet Flight 592 crashed in the Florida Everglades in May 1996 after a fire developed in a cargo compartment. Chemical oxygen generators loaded as company material became central to the investigation.
mechanism: The article must trace removal, handling, packaging, labeling, loading and activation of the generators, and explain what the cargo compartment could and could not contain.
system: The case asks how responsibility moves among airline, contractor, shipping personnel and regulator when hazardous items pass through several organizational boundaries.
memory: The low-cost airline narrative can oversimplify the record; the more precise story concerns controls over outsourced maintenance and company materials.

title: Herald of Free Enterprise: An Open Door and a Company-Wide Failure
dek: The 1987 ferry capsize became a defining case in moving beyond blame of the last operator.
event: The roll-on/roll-off ferry Herald of Free Enterprise capsized shortly after leaving Zeebrugge in March 1987 with its bow doors open. The inquiry examined ship stability, departure checks and management practices.
mechanism: The account must reconstruct loading, trim, door status, acceleration and flooding while separating the immediate omission from conditions that made the omission undetected.
system: The disaster asks how a company designs confirmation, staffing and responsibility for a safety-critical state that is not visible from the bridge.
memory: The open doors are a simple image; the inquiry's description of a wider disease of sloppiness is the harder organizational record to test and explain.

title: Estonia: The Bow Visor, the Car Deck and a Contested Record
dek: The 1994 Baltic ferry sinking remains both a technical investigation and a dispute over access, evidence and memory.
event: The ferry Estonia sank in the Baltic Sea in September 1994 during severe weather. The official investigation focused on failure of the bow visor and water entering the vehicle deck, while later examinations and disputes continued.
mechanism: The article must distinguish established damage, modeled flooding, survivor testimony and claims raised by later imagery, avoiding both automatic deference and unsupported conspiracy.
system: Estonia asks how international investigations preserve evidence, explain uncertainty and maintain legitimacy when the wreck is inaccessible and families contest decisions about further examination.
memory: The scale of loss and continuing controversy can crowd out careful reading of which questions were answered, reopened or never testable.

source.title: Sinking of the MS Estonia overview

title: Costa Concordia: Route Deviation, Damage and the Delayed Abandonment
dek: The 2012 grounding connects bridge decisions with flooding, passenger communication and a complex evacuation.
event: The cruise ship Costa Concordia struck rocks near Giglio in January 2012, flooded and rolled onto its side. The article follows the route deviation, damage assessment, communication and timing of evacuation.
mechanism: The chronology must use voyage data, bridge audio and official findings to identify when the ship's condition was known and when information reached passengers and authorities.
system: The event asks how command, company operations and shore rescue coordinate when a large passenger vessel loses power and stability close to land.
memory: The captain's conduct dominates public memory, potentially reducing thousands of individual evacuation problems to a single morality play.

title: Sewol: Cargo, Stability and the Order to Stay Put
dek: The 2014 South Korean ferry disaster joined vessel modification, cargo control and institutional response.
event: The ferry Sewol capsized in April 2014 while carrying students and other passengers. Investigations and trials examined overloading, securing of cargo, vessel modification, crew actions and the rescue response.
mechanism: The article must distinguish stability calculations, cargo records, steering events, announcements and evacuation timing while noting differences between technical and criminal findings.
system: Sewol asks how regulators, operators and emergency agencies manage risk when certification, enforcement and rescue each depend on information produced by another institution.
memory: The instruction for passengers to remain in place is unforgettable, but the full record reaches backward into vessel ownership and forward into state accountability.

title: Derbyshire: A Lost Bulk Carrier and the Evidence Found Years Later
dek: The 1980 loss of the Derbyshire became a long investigation into hatch covers, storm loading and access to a deep wreck.
event: The British bulk carrier Derbyshire disappeared during Typhoon Orchid in September 1980. Years later, deep-sea surveys and a reopened inquiry examined how water could have entered and how the ship progressively failed.
mechanism: The article must distinguish early hypotheses from findings made possible by locating and imaging the wreck, and explain the sequence without overstating what broken debris can prove.
system: Derbyshire asks how casualty investigation changes when the primary evidence is unavailable for years and when families must campaign to reopen the record.
memory: The ship was initially another vessel lost in a storm; the later evidence turned that natural-hazard explanation into a design and regulation inquiry.

title: Ocean Ranger: Ballast Controls in a Winter Storm
dek: The 1982 loss of the offshore drilling unit exposed control-room flooding, training and evacuation limits.
event: The semi-submersible drilling unit Ocean Ranger sank off Newfoundland in February 1982 during a severe storm. Investigators examined water entering the ballast-control room, unexpected valve movement, stability and evacuation.
mechanism: The narrative must trace broken windows, control-panel behavior, ballast changes and the unit's increasing list while separating confirmed signals from radio interpretations.
system: Ocean Ranger asks whether crews are trained for opaque control-system failures and whether lifesaving equipment is usable in the sea states that make abandonment necessary.
memory: The storm is prominent in remembrance; the vulnerability of a control room and the mismatch between evacuation plans and North Atlantic conditions deserve equal weight.

title: Alexander L. Kielland: A Fatigue Crack Across an Offshore Structure
dek: The 1980 platform capsize linked one welded detail to redundancy, stability and evacuation.
event: The Alexander L. Kielland accommodation platform capsized in the North Sea in March 1980 after structural failure in one bracing system. The event became a study of fatigue, inspection and lifesaving arrangements.
mechanism: The article should explain crack initiation at a welded connection, brace failure, loss of a support column and capsize without presenting the first crack as the only relevant design issue.
system: The case asks how redundant an offshore structure really is when one connection can change the load path faster than detection or evacuation can respond.
memory: The metallurgical origin is memorable to engineers, while survival also depended on alarms, list, launchable boats and conditions on deck.

title: Lac-Mégantic: An Unattended Train and a Town Below the Grade
dek: The 2013 derailment joined securement, locomotive fire, tank cars and regulatory oversight.
event: An unattended freight train carrying crude oil rolled downhill and derailed in Lac-Mégantic, Quebec, in July 2013. The resulting fire devastated the town center and exposed several layers of rail-safety governance.
mechanism: The chronology must follow train securement, the locomotive fire, shutdown, loss of air brakes, movement, derailment and tank-car failures using official evidence.
system: The event asks how crew staffing, operating rules, company finances, regulator surveillance and tank-car standards combine around a high-consequence route.
memory: The runaway train is the dominant image; the regulatory and commercial system that placed volatile cargo above a town is less visually immediate.

title: Eschede: A Wheel Tire and the High-Speed System Around It
dek: The 1998 German rail disaster linked wheel design, inspection and infrastructure interaction.
event: A high-speed Intercity Express train derailed near Eschede in June 1998 after failure of a wheel component, then struck bridge infrastructure. The disaster made component design and detection part of a larger systems inquiry.
mechanism: The article must trace fatigue in the wheel tire, its interaction with track equipment, derailment and bridge collapse while carefully distinguishing sequence from causal contribution.
system: Eschede asks how design changes borrowed from other rail contexts are validated for high-speed service and how inspections detect cracks in safety-critical rotating parts.
memory: The collapsed bridge dominates photographs, but the initiating wheel and the organizational path that approved it carry much of the transferable evidence.

title: Quintinshill: Signaling, Shift Change and a Wartime Railway
dek: The 1915 collision in Scotland grew from operating irregularities into fire and mass loss aboard a troop train.
event: Multiple trains collided at Quintinshill near Gretna Green in May 1915, and fire consumed wooden carriages carrying soldiers. The disaster involved block signaling, a local train positioned on the main line and incomplete safety reminders.
mechanism: The draft must reconstruct train positions, signal indications, the shift handover and the later collision and fire, using inquiry records rather than criminal verdicts alone.
system: Quintinshill asks how informal workarounds become normalized and how a shift-change routine can defeat formal signaling protections.
memory: Wartime loss and individual blame shape the story, while the everyday operating practices that preceded the collision need separate examination.

title: Apollo 1: A Ground Test Inside a Flight Capsule
dek: The 1967 fire exposed how atmosphere, materials, hatch design and test planning created a lethal configuration.
event: A fire inside Apollo spacecraft 012 during a launch-pad test in January 1967 killed astronauts Virgil Grissom, Edward White and Roger Chaffee. The investigation examined the pure-oxygen atmosphere, ignition possibilities, combustible materials, wiring and the inward-opening hatch.
mechanism: The article must distinguish the unidentified exact ignition point from the conditions that allowed rapid fire growth and prevented escape, following the review board's stated evidence limits.
system: Apollo 1 asks why a configuration treated as a test condition carried hazards different from flight and how schedule, change control and contractor-agency communication governed those hazards.
memory: The tragedy is commonly positioned as a prelude to lunar success; this article keeps the crew and the management findings from becoming merely a lesson on the way to victory.

source.title: NASA Apollo 1 mission and investigation archive

title: Soyuz 1: A Troubled Mission and the Final Parachute Sequence
dek: The 1967 mission ended in a fatal landing failure after problems accumulated in orbit.
event: Cosmonaut Vladimir Komarov died when Soyuz 1 crashed during return in April 1967 after a mission marked by spacecraft malfunctions. The article separates documented orbital problems from the parachute failure during descent.
mechanism: The draft must verify deployment sequence, container behavior, reserve-parachute interaction and landing-system design through technical histories rather than repeated dramatic anecdotes.
system: Soyuz 1 raises questions about test evidence, launch pressure and how dissent was recorded inside a secretive program where later memoirs carry uneven reliability.
memory: Stories of final transmissions and political pressure often circulate without primary support, making source discipline central to any retelling.

title: Soyuz 11: A Valve, a Pressure Loss and a Cabin Without Suits
dek: The 1971 return from Salyut 1 exposed how spacecraft capacity and pressure protection were traded.
event: The Soyuz 11 crew died during return to Earth in June 1971 after their capsule depressurized. Recovery teams found the spacecraft landed automatically, shifting investigation toward a ventilation valve and the absence of pressure suits.
mechanism: The account must establish separation events, valve opening, pressure decay and the crew's possible response from telemetry and design records, not from invented cockpit dialogue.
system: The event asks how seating capacity, suit use and automatic landing design distributed risk, and how one valve's behavior was protected against a dynamic separation environment.
memory: Success aboard the first space station can frame the deaths as a return accident detached from the program choices that shaped cabin survival.

title: Skylab 1: The Shield That Tore Away During Launch
dek: The 1973 anomaly threatened America's first space station before its crew ever reached orbit.
event: During Skylab's launch in May 1973, aerodynamic forces tore away its micrometeoroid shield and damaged its solar-array system. Engineers and astronauts then improvised ways to control temperature and restore power in orbit.
mechanism: The article must trace the launch anomalies, shield breakup, array damage and thermal consequences using telemetry and the investigation's load analysis.
system: Skylab asks how a protective structure can introduce a launch hazard, and how mission recovery balances incomplete ground testing with crew exposure during repair.
memory: The successful repair makes an inspiring ending, but it can obscure the design assumptions and close calls that put the station at risk before rescue began.

source.title: NASA Readings in Systems Engineering, Skylab 1 anomaly section

title: Nedelin: A Missile Test, a Pad Full of People and Years of Secrecy
dek: The 1960 Baikonur explosion joins hazardous launch preparation with political pressure and suppressed records.
event: An R-16 missile exploded during launch preparations at Baikonur in October 1960, killing many people gathered around the pad. The catastrophe was concealed for decades and later became known by the name of Marshal Mitrofan Nedelin.
mechanism: The article must verify electrical sequencing, propellant conditions, work taking place on the fueled missile and casualty estimates through declassified or scholarly records.
system: The event asks how schedule pressure, command presence and secrecy can concentrate personnel around a system whose hazards are still active.
memory: Long suppression created a space filled by rumor; later openness does not automatically resolve conflicting counts or dramatic anecdotes.

title: Mars Polar Lander: The Signal That Never Returned
dek: The 1999 loss forced investigators to infer a failure from design and test evidence without wreckage or telemetry.
event: NASA lost contact with Mars Polar Lander during descent in December 1999. With no post-entry telemetry and no recovered hardware, investigators evaluated plausible failure modes through design, software and test records.
mechanism: The draft must distinguish the leading hypothesis involving landing-leg signals from a proven cause, and explain exactly what data ended before descent.
system: The case asks how a mission verifies transient software and sensor behavior when testing cannot reproduce the complete flight environment and when telemetry is intentionally interrupted.
memory: A concise probable cause can sound definitive; the absence of direct evidence is itself the most important condition of the investigation.

title: Genesis: The Sensor Installed Backwards
dek: The 2004 sample-return crash showed how a small orientation error can bypass analysis, test and recovery plans.
event: NASA's Genesis sample-return capsule struck the Utah desert in September 2004 after its parachutes failed to deploy. Investigation traced the failure to gravity switches installed in the wrong orientation.
mechanism: The article must explain what the switches were intended to sense, how orientation prevented the sequence and which tests could have revealed the problem without overstating the condition of recovered samples.
system: Genesis asks how drawing interpretation, component heritage, inspection and end-to-end testing interact when a simple error sits inside a one-time sequence.
memory: The backwards sensor offers a memorable punch line, but it should lead into the verification system that accepted it rather than close the story.

title: NOAA-N Prime: The Satellite That Fell During Maintenance
dek: A 2003 clean-room accident turned missing fasteners and undocumented work into an expensive recovery.
event: The NOAA-N Prime weather satellite fell from a handling cart in a Lockheed Martin facility in September 2003 while it was being rotated. Bolts needed to secure the spacecraft were absent after an earlier operation.
mechanism: The reporting must establish which fasteners were removed, how configuration status was recorded, what checks preceded movement and how damage and repair costs were assessed.
system: The accident asks how maintenance handoffs preserve temporary configuration changes and whether a physical safeguard depends on memory across teams and shifts.
memory: The image of a satellite on the floor invites ridicule, but the more useful record concerns configuration control and institutional learning from an apparently simple omission.

title: DART: An Autonomous Rendezvous That Ended in Contact
dek: NASA's 2005 demonstration vehicle exhausted propellant and collided with its target after navigation errors.
event: NASA's Demonstration for Autonomous Rendezvous Technology mission approached a target satellite in April 2005 but experienced navigation and propellant problems and made unplanned contact. The mission ended before completing its objectives.
mechanism: The article must trace sensor interpretation, relative-navigation estimates, commanded maneuvers, propellant use and contact using the mishap report.
system: DART asks how autonomous systems expose uncertainty, enforce keep-out zones and transition to a safe mode when their internal state estimate diverges from reality.
memory: Autonomy can make the failure sound like a machine acting alone; the design, simulation and oversight choices remain human institutional work.

title: SL-1: A Control Rod, a Prompt Critical Excursion and an Isolated Reactor
dek: The 1961 Idaho accident became a difficult investigation of reactor design, maintenance and an uncertain human action.
event: The Stationary Low-Power Reactor Number One was destroyed during maintenance in January 1961, killing the three operators present. Investigation concluded that a central control rod had been withdrawn far beyond its normal position, producing a rapid power excursion.
mechanism: The article must explain control-rod worth, manual movement, steam generation and vessel motion while refusing to present a disputed reason for the rod withdrawal as established fact.
system: SL-1 asks why one manually movable component could introduce such reactivity and how staffing, maintenance procedure and reactor design shared responsibility.
memory: Speculation about motive often overwhelms the engineering evidence; the article must protect the boundary between physical finding and unknowable intent.

title: Tokaimura: A Bucket, a Precipitation Tank and a Criticality
dek: The 1999 Japanese fuel-processing accident linked improvised work practice to nuclear geometry.
event: A criticality accident occurred at a JCO fuel-processing plant in Tokaimura in September 1999 after workers added enriched uranium solution to a vessel. The reaction continued intermittently until responders altered the surrounding conditions.
mechanism: The draft must explain concentration, vessel geometry, neutron moderation and the sequence used to stop the reaction without turning technical explanation into a claim about individual understanding.
system: Tokaimura asks how unofficial procedures become normal production practice and how regulators assess work that has drifted away from the licensed process.
memory: The use of buckets is visually shocking, but the deeper record concerns organizational approval of shortcuts and the absence of criticality emergency preparation.

title: Donora: Five Days of Smog and a Public-Health Turning Point
dek: The 1948 air-pollution episode in Pennsylvania connected weather, industrial emissions and community health.
event: A temperature inversion trapped industrial pollution over Donora, Pennsylvania, in October 1948, producing severe illness and deaths during several days of dense smog. The episode later became part of the case for federal air-pollution research and law.
mechanism: The article must distinguish measured or reconstructed emissions, meteorology, clinical reports and mortality estimates, and should not assign individual deaths without examining health records.
system: Donora asks how a company town recognizes environmental illness when employment, local authority, medical observation and emissions are institutionally intertwined.
memory: The event is remembered as a legislative catalyst, which can compress the experiences of residents into a prologue for later clean-air policy.

title: Cuyahoga 1969: The River Fire That Was Not the First
dek: The famous Cleveland fire became an environmental symbol partly because earlier pollution had already built the record.
event: The Cuyahoga River caught fire in Cleveland in June 1969, but industrial river fires had occurred there before. The episode's political significance came from timing, accumulated concern and later use of the image as an environmental symbol.
mechanism: The article must identify what burned, what evidence survives from the relatively small 1969 fire and which commonly reproduced photographs actually depict earlier events.
system: The systems question is how municipal sewage, industrial discharge, navigation and fragmented water authority allowed pollution to become normal infrastructure.
memory: The iconic photograph and claim that the fire created the EPA are often repeated too simply; chronology can show a broader movement and policy process.

title: Santa Barbara: A Blowout Beneath the Channel
dek: The 1969 offshore spill connected drilling decisions, seabed pathways and the politics of coastal protection.
event: An offshore well blowout in the Santa Barbara Channel in January 1969 released oil that reached the California coast. Oil also migrated through fractures beyond the well bore, complicating attempts to stop the discharge.
mechanism: The article must reconstruct drilling depth, casing decisions, blowout control and seabed seepage from official investigation rather than treating the spill as one leaking pipe.
system: The event asks how federal leasing, operator decisions, geological uncertainty and coastal communities shared authority over offshore risk.
memory: The spill is commonly called a birthplace of modern environmentalism, which should be tested against the movements and legislation already underway.

title: Torrey Canyon: Grounding, Detergent and the First Super-Spill Response
dek: The 1967 tanker grounding forced Britain and France to improvise environmental response at sea and on shore.
event: The tanker Torrey Canyon grounded near Cornwall in March 1967 and released oil across the English Channel. Authorities used detergents and bombing in efforts to limit the spill, creating additional questions about ecological harm.
mechanism: The article must separate the navigation and grounding sequence from the breakup, oil movement and effects of response chemicals, using contemporary technical assessments.
system: Torrey Canyon asks what happens when vessel ownership, flag, cargo, coastal impact and response authority cross national and legal boundaries.
memory: The extraordinary bombing effort is memorable, but the improvised use of toxic dispersants and the absence of prepared international liability systems carry the longer legacy.

title: Amoco Cadiz: Steering Failure and a Coastline Under Oil
dek: The 1978 tanker loss off Brittany became a case about towing delay, total cargo loss and transnational liability.
event: The tanker Amoco Cadiz lost steering and grounded off Brittany in March 1978, eventually breaking apart and releasing its cargo. The response and litigation extended far beyond the initial mechanical failure.
mechanism: The account must trace steering loss, assistance negotiations, tow attempts, weather and grounding, while distinguishing immediate response decisions from later legal findings.
system: The spill asks how commercial salvage, ship operation, coastal authority and corporate ownership align when delay carries environmental consequences.
memory: The blackened coast became the visual record; the hours of failed control and negotiation before grounding are the less familiar systems story.

title: Ixtoc I: Nine Months of Oil From a Shallow-Water Blowout
dek: The 1979 Gulf of Mexico blowout tested drilling control and spill response long before Deepwater Horizon.
event: The Ixtoc I exploratory well blew out in the Bay of Campeche in June 1979 and released oil for months before it was brought under control. The spill affected waters and shorelines across national boundaries.
mechanism: The draft must establish drilling conditions, loss of circulation, blowout-preventer operation and the sequence of capping and relief-well efforts from technical records.
system: Ixtoc asks how offshore operators and governments learn from a prolonged uncontrolled well and whether those lessons remain available across companies, countries and decades.
memory: Deepwater Horizon now dominates Gulf spill memory, making Ixtoc easy to treat as a historical footnote rather than a prior full-scale warning.

title: Exxon Valdez: Navigation, Fatigue and the Limits of Preparedness
dek: The 1989 grounding made staffing, traffic oversight and an unready spill plan part of one record.
event: The tanker Exxon Valdez grounded on Bligh Reef in Prince William Sound in March 1989 and released crude oil into a remote coastal environment. Investigation and litigation examined navigation, watchkeeping and response readiness.
mechanism: The article must reconstruct the vessel's departure from the traffic lane, bridge staffing, turn sequence, grounding and early containment using official records rather than later corporate shorthand.
system: The case asks whether a regional oil-transport system had response capacity proportionate to the cargo and geography it depended on.
memory: One captain's conduct often carries the public story, while crew workload, traffic services and promised response equipment form a wider institutional record.

title: Deepwater Horizon: The Well, the Barriers and the Decisions Before the Blowout
dek: The 2010 disaster joined well design, temporary abandonment and emergency systems across multiple companies.
event: The Deepwater Horizon drilling rig exploded in April 2010 after hydrocarbons entered the well and reached the rig. The blowout killed workers, sank the rig and led to a prolonged spill from the Macondo well.
mechanism: The article must trace cement barriers, pressure-test interpretation, displacement of drilling fluid, influx detection, blowout-preventer performance and ignition as distinct stages.
system: The event asks how operator, drilling contractor, service companies and regulators shared decisions while no single organization controlled every barrier.
memory: Images of the surface fire and underwater leak can split the story into accident and spill; the same well-control chain connects them.

title: Kingston: The Coal-Ash Impoundment That Moved Like a Flood
dek: The 2008 Tennessee spill turned a utility waste pond into a national question about ash storage.
event: A coal-fly-ash impoundment at the Tennessee Valley Authority's Kingston plant failed in December 2008, releasing a large volume of ash slurry across nearby land and waterways. Cleanup and worker-health disputes continued for years.
mechanism: The article must trace foundation conditions, upstream construction, water levels and progressive failure using engineering reports, while separately examining cleanup exposure claims.
system: Kingston asks why combustion waste was managed through dam-like structures under a regulatory category different from conventional hazardous waste or water dams.
memory: The gray flood is visually clear; the classification of ash, the workforce that removed it and the long litigation record are less immediate.

source.title: Kingston Fossil Plant coal fly ash slurry spill overview

title: Flint: A Water-Source Switch and the Missing Corrosion Control
dek: The Flint crisis joined treatment chemistry, sampling rules, fiscal governance and residents' ignored evidence.
event: Flint, Michigan, changed its drinking-water source in 2014 and distributed water without adequate corrosion control, contributing to lead release from plumbing. Residents' complaints and independent testing challenged official assurances.
mechanism: The article must distinguish water-source quality, treatment decisions, pipe chemistry, sampling practice, blood-lead evidence and the separate Legionnaires' outbreak.
system: Flint asks how emergency financial management, state regulation, local utilities and federal oversight divided authority while residents carried the exposure.
memory: A single decision to switch water sources is easy to identify, but the prolonged dismissal of household evidence is central to understanding why exposure continued.

title: WorldCom: When Ordinary Network Costs Became Assets
dek: The accounting fraud transformed recurring line costs into reported profit and exposed failures across management, audit and governance.
event: WorldCom disclosed major accounting irregularities in 2002 after internal work uncovered costs that had been improperly capitalized. The collapse became one of the defining corporate failures of the post-dot-com period.
mechanism: The article must explain line costs, capitalization entries, reserve releases and earnings effects using SEC and court records without implying that every employee or transaction shared the same intent.
system: WorldCom asks how executive pressure, general-ledger access, internal audit, external audit and board oversight interacted when simple entries produced enormous aggregate effects.
memory: The size of the bankruptcy can overshadow the mundane mechanism: repeated accounting entries that bypassed the economic meaning of an operating expense.

title: HealthSouth: The Meeting Where Earnings Gaps Became Entries
dek: The HealthSouth case showed how many small asset entries could be used to bridge a corporate earnings target.
event: Federal authorities accused HealthSouth executives of systematically inflating earnings before the fraud became public in 2003. Accounts of the scheme describe meetings, target gaps and entries designed to avoid auditor attention.
mechanism: The article must separate allegations, guilty pleas, trial outcomes and SEC findings, and verify how entries were divided, recorded and concealed.
system: HealthSouth asks how a finance function can normalize repeated fraudulent adjustment when participation is distributed and performance expectations come from the top.
memory: The chief executive's acquittal on criminal charges complicates any simple story and requires careful separation of company fraud from individual verdicts.

title: Madoff: The Statements, the Custody and the Checks That Did Not Close
dek: The Ponzi scheme persisted through fabricated trading records and repeated failures to verify assets independently.
event: Bernard Madoff's investment-advisory business collapsed in December 2008 and was revealed as a long-running Ponzi scheme. The record includes fabricated statements, feeder funds, warnings and multiple regulatory examinations.
mechanism: The article must distinguish reported returns from actual cash flows, explain custody and trade verification, and separate criminal admissions from later estimates of losses and recoveries.
system: The case asks why regulators, auditors, banks and sophisticated investors did not independently close the loop between claimed trades, held assets and reported performance.
memory: Madoff's personality can dominate the narrative, while the institutional value lies in the specific verification steps that were absent or ineffective.

title: MF Global: Sovereign-Debt Bets and the Customer-Money Shortfall
dek: The 2011 brokerage collapse linked liquidity pressure, repo accounting and controls over segregated funds.
event: MF Global filed for bankruptcy in October 2011 after large European sovereign-debt positions and a loss of market confidence strained the firm. A shortfall in customer property intensified the failure.
mechanism: The article must explain repo-to-maturity transactions, margin and liquidity demands, transfers near bankruptcy and the later recovery of customer funds without conflating accounting treatment with economic risk.
system: MF Global asks how treasury operations protect segregated customer assets during a rapidly deteriorating liquidity crisis when many transfers occur under time pressure.
memory: The identity of the chief executive and the missing-money headline can obscure the operational control problem inside the final days.

title: Wells Fargo: Sales Targets and Accounts Customers Did Not Request
dek: The unauthorized-accounts scandal connected branch-level conduct to incentive design and executive oversight.
event: Investigations found that Wells Fargo employees opened or applied for accounts and services without customer authorization over a period of years. Enforcement actions examined sales pressure, complaints, terminations and management reporting.
mechanism: The article must separate different products, time periods and legal findings, and verify counts as estimates changed through settlements and reviews.
system: The case asks how incentive targets, local supervision, complaint channels, risk functions and board reporting convert widespread employee actions into an organizational failure.
memory: The phrase fake accounts is compact but imprecise; customers experienced several distinct forms of unauthorized enrollment and financial harm.

title: Volkswagen: Software That Recognized the Test
dek: The diesel-emissions scandal turned calibration code, laboratory cycles and corporate claims into evidence.
event: Regulators disclosed in 2015 that Volkswagen diesel vehicles used software strategies that produced different emissions behavior under testing and ordinary driving. The case spread across models, countries and legal regimes.
mechanism: The article must explain test detection, engine-control behavior and measured emissions without assuming one implementation applied identically to every affected vehicle.
system: Volkswagen asks how software review, emissions certification, supplier relationships, engineering hierarchy and sales strategy interact when compliance exists partly in code.
memory: The label defeat device is legally powerful, but the institutional story requires tracing who knew which calibrations, when, and how objections moved through the company.

title: LTCM: Convergence Trades, Leverage and a Private Rescue
dek: The 1998 hedge-fund crisis showed how models and crowded positions can turn market stress into a system problem.
event: Long-Term Capital Management suffered severe losses in 1998 after market relationships moved against highly leveraged positions. The Federal Reserve Bank of New York facilitated discussions that produced a private-sector recapitalization.
mechanism: The article must distinguish model assumptions, leverage, liquidity, counterparty exposures and the terms of the rescue without portraying the Federal Reserve as directly paying the fund's losses.
system: LTCM asks how many counterparties can each manage bilateral risk while collectively creating a liquidation problem no one sees in full.
memory: Nobel laureates and mathematical models make a compelling morality tale, but crowded trades, financing terms and dealer exposure are the more operational record.

title: The Savings and Loan Crisis: Deregulation, Insolvency and Delayed Closure
dek: The U.S. thrift crisis grew through interest-rate shocks, expanded powers, weak supervision and institutions kept open after insolvency.
event: Hundreds of U.S. savings and loan institutions failed during the 1980s and early 1990s, producing a costly federal resolution. The crisis combined a changed interest-rate environment with deregulation, risky investment and delayed recognition of losses.
mechanism: The article must distinguish economic insolvency, accounting treatment, deposit insurance, fraud cases and resolution costs rather than treating every failed thrift as the same scheme.
system: The crisis asks what happens when institutions can take larger risks while deposit guarantees remain and supervisors lack resources or political support to close them promptly.
memory: A few notorious executives dominate public recollection, obscuring the interaction between macroeconomic shocks and policy choices across an entire sector.

title: Banco Ambrosiano: Offshore Entities, Missing Records and a Bank Collapse
dek: The 1982 Italian banking failure sits inside a web of offshore companies, political influence and contested responsibility.
event: Banco Ambrosiano collapsed in 1982 after losses and exposures linked to offshore entities became untenable. The death of chairman Roberto Calvi and the Vatican bank's relationships with parts of the network made the case unusually contested.
mechanism: The article must separate documented loans, guarantees, regulatory findings, settlements and criminal allegations from speculation surrounding Calvi's death.
system: The collapse asks how banking supervision follows risk through nominally separate foreign entities and relationships involving institutions with unusual legal status.
memory: Mystery and conspiracy narratives attract attention, while the balance-sheet pathways and jurisdictional gaps are more difficult to reconstruct.

title: Equitable Life: Guarantees That Became More Expensive Than Expected
dek: The British insurer's crisis connected long-dated guarantees, falling interest rates and policyholder fairness.
event: Equitable Life closed to new business in 2000 after legal and financial pressure related to guaranteed annuity-rate policies. The crisis affected policy values and produced long-running disputes over regulation and compensation.
mechanism: The article must explain the guarantees, bonus policy, interest-rate environment and court decision without turning actuarial assumptions into certainty about later losses.
system: The case asks how a mutual insurer allocates costs among policyholder groups when past guarantees become expensive and no external shareholders absorb the change.
memory: The absence of a dramatic bankruptcy can make Equitable Life less visible, even though the governance and regulatory consequences lasted for years.

title: Grenfell Tower: Refurbishment, Compartmentation and a Failed Safety System
dek: The 2017 London fire connected exterior materials, building regulation, resident warnings and emergency doctrine.
event: Fire spread rapidly through Grenfell Tower in June 2017 after beginning in a flat. The public inquiry examined exterior cladding and insulation, cavity barriers, windows, internal systems, regulation and the emergency response.
mechanism: The article must distinguish the initiating appliance fire from the pathways that carried fire and smoke through the building, using inquiry findings for each component.
system: Grenfell asks how testing, product marketing, design, approval, inspection, ownership and firefighting doctrine formed a system that residents had repeatedly warned was unsafe.
memory: The cladding is a necessary focus but not a complete explanation; the inquiry record reaches through decades of regulatory and institutional choices.

title: Ronan Point: A Gas Explosion and Progressive Collapse
dek: The 1968 tower collapse changed how engineers considered disproportionate failure in prefabricated buildings.
event: A gas explosion in a flat at Ronan Point in London in May 1968 caused sections of the prefabricated tower to collapse from the top downward. The event exposed weakness in connections among large concrete panels.
