mechanism: The article must explain the local explosion, loss of wall support and vertical propagation while distinguishing original construction from later strengthening work.
system: Ronan Point asks how standardized housing production, building approval and pressure for rapid construction addressed structural robustness beyond normal loads.
memory: The domestic scale of the initiating explosion makes the collapse seem freakish; the important record is why the building could not contain a local failure.

title: Hartford Civic Center: The Space-Frame Roof That Sagged Overnight
dek: The 1978 collapse occurred hours after a crowd left, exposing analysis and review weaknesses without a mass casualty event.
event: The roof of the Hartford Civic Center Coliseum collapsed under snow in January 1978, hours after the building had held thousands of spectators. Investigation examined the space-frame design, computer analysis and construction deviations.
mechanism: The article must separate design assumptions, member behavior, connection details, observed deflection and snow loading rather than presenting snow as the sole cause.
system: The case asks how novel computer-aided analysis is independently checked and how visible deformation is interpreted once a building is in service.
memory: Because the building was empty, the collapse is less remembered than deadlier failures, although the near miss makes its review lessons unusually important.

title: Champlain Towers South: Deterioration, Recertification and Collapse
dek: The 2021 Surfside collapse brought aging concrete, repair planning and local oversight into one investigation.
event: Part of Champlain Towers South in Surfside, Florida, collapsed in June 2021. Investigators examined structural design, deterioration, waterproofing, pool-deck conditions, inspection and repairs that had not yet begun.
mechanism: The article must separate observed deterioration, engineering recommendations, hypothesized initiation zones and findings confirmed by physical and modeling evidence.
system: Surfside asks how condominium governance, reserve funding, engineering advice and municipal recertification manage expensive risks that worsen slowly but can fail suddenly.
memory: Images of the collapse are immediate; the years of correspondence, concrete damage and deferred decisions require a slower documentary narrative.

title: Iroquois Theatre: Fireproof Claims and Exits That Did Not Work
dek: The 1903 Chicago fire exposed the distance between a building's reputation and its actual evacuation systems.
event: Fire swept through Chicago's Iroquois Theatre during a performance in December 1903. The building had been promoted as fireproof, yet stage protection, exits, doors and crowd movement failed under real conditions.
mechanism: The article must reconstruct ignition and stage-fire development, smoke and flame movement, door operation and exterior escape conditions from inquest and contemporary records.
system: The event asks how inspection, licensing, commercial promotion and opening schedules allowed an entertainment venue to operate before protective systems were complete or usable.
memory: The word fireproof became an indictment after the fire; the article should show exactly which protections the claim implied and which were absent.

title: Cocoanut Grove: A Nightclub Fire and the Doors Between People and Safety
dek: The 1942 Boston fire transformed knowledge about exits, interior finishes, smoke and mass-casualty care.
event: A fast-moving fire at Boston's Cocoanut Grove nightclub in November 1942 killed hundreds of patrons. Investigations and medical studies examined ignition, decorations, crowding, locked or obscured exits and treatment of burns and smoke exposure.
mechanism: The article must distinguish the uncertain ignition source from well-documented evacuation barriers and fire spread, and verify occupancy and casualty figures across records.
system: Cocoanut Grove asks how licensing, enforcement and social influence shape the gap between posted safety requirements and a venue's actual nightly configuration.
memory: Stories about one match or one employee can dominate, while doors, occupancy and material choices made the consequences much larger than the ignition alone.

title: King's Cross: A Small Escalator Fire and the Trench Effect
dek: The 1987 London Underground fire changed understanding of flame behavior on inclined escalators.
event: A fire beneath a wooden escalator at King's Cross St Pancras station in November 1987 suddenly intensified and spread into the ticket hall. Investigation used experiments to explain the rapid flame development.
mechanism: The article must trace ignition, concealed burning, airflow, escalator geometry and flashover, distinguishing the later trench-effect model from what responders knew that night.
system: The event asks how repeated small fires can be normalized within an organization and how station staffing and emergency command respond when an incident changes scale abruptly.
memory: The scientific explanation is striking, but it should not eclipse the history of prior escalator fires and institutional assumptions that they would remain manageable.

title: Bradford City: Litter, Timber and a Stand Evacuated in Minutes
dek: The 1985 stadium fire exposed how an old grandstand and accumulated debris could create rapid flame spread.
event: Fire spread through the main stand at Bradford City's Valley Parade stadium in May 1985 during a football match. Timber construction and debris beneath seating contributed to rapid development as spectators tried to reach the field and exits.
mechanism: The article must reconstruct the first visible smoke, fire growth, roof involvement and evacuation routes while separating confirmed ignition evidence from later speculation.
system: The case asks how older venues remain in use while known renovation plans, housekeeping and crowd-safety requirements await action.
memory: Broadcast footage makes the speed unforgettable, but the pre-fire condition of the stand and unfinished replacement plans are essential context.

title: Hillsborough: Crowd Safety, Police Decisions and the Long Correction of the Record
dek: The 1989 disaster became as much a history of evidence and official narrative as of stadium design.
event: A fatal crowd crush occurred at Hillsborough stadium in April 1989 during an FA Cup semifinal. Later inquiries and inquests overturned early narratives that blamed supporters and examined police command, stadium layout and emergency response.
mechanism: The article must reconstruct turnstile congestion, gate opening, movement into central pens, barrier loading and emergency actions from the corrected evidentiary record.
system: Hillsborough asks how authorities create an official story after disaster and how families, journalists and independent review can expose alteration, omission or misinterpretation of evidence.
memory: The long campaign for truth is inseparable from the event because the original public account shaped accountability for decades.

title: Love Parade 2010: A Single Access Route and Crowd Compression
dek: The Duisburg disaster exposed how event planning, route geometry and divided authority shape crowd risk.
event: A deadly crowd disaster occurred at the Love Parade in Duisburg in July 2010 near a tunnel and ramp used for access to the festival grounds. Investigations and trials examined crowd flow, planning and operational decisions.
mechanism: The article must map entry and exit streams, barriers, police lines, density, communication and the locations of falls without describing all deaths through one simple mechanism.
system: The event asks how organizer, city, police and contractors approve a plan when responsibility is distributed but physical capacity is not.
memory: The word stampede can wrongly imply irrational movement; the record instead requires attention to constrained geometry and system-created density.

title: AT&T 1990: One Software Update and a Cascading Telephone Outage
dek: A timing interaction in switch software propagated through a network designed to recover automatically.
event: A major AT&T long-distance network outage occurred in January 1990 after updated switching software interacted with recovery messages across the network. Switches repeatedly reset and disrupted calls for hours.
mechanism: The article must explain the message sequence, timing window, reset behavior and rollout scope without turning a few lines of code into the whole causal account.
system: The outage asks how identical software across many nodes can convert local recovery behavior into a common-mode failure and how deployment strategy limits that risk.
memory: The famous coding bug is memorable, while synchronized architecture, testing assumptions and nationwide rollout made its consequences possible.

title: The 2003 Northeast Blackout: Trees, Alarms and a Cascading Grid
dek: The outage grew from local line contacts and failed situational awareness into a regional loss of power.
event: A cascading power outage affected parts of the northeastern United States and Ontario in August 2003. Investigation examined transmission lines contacting trees, alarm-system failures and the progression of grid instability.
mechanism: The article must follow line trips, state-estimator and alarm behavior, operator understanding, power flows and protective actions in time order.
system: The blackout asks how regional reliability is governed when individual utilities operate connected equipment and depend on shared situational awareness.
memory: Trees are often offered as the cause, but vegetation contact became catastrophic only through failed alarms, inadequate analysis and cascading interdependence.

title: Knight Capital: Forty-Five Minutes of Uncontrolled Orders
dek: A 2012 software deployment activated obsolete behavior and generated a market-loss spiral.
event: Knight Capital suffered severe losses in August 2012 after a software deployment caused systems to send unintended orders into the market. The incident unfolded rapidly across servers running inconsistent code.
mechanism: The article must explain deployment state, reused flags, server differences, order generation and attempts to diagnose the problem using regulatory findings.
system: The case asks how a financial firm controls releases when software has direct authority to commit capital at machine speed and rollback is not instantaneous.
memory: The loss total and short duration make the incident sound like a freak bug; deployment discipline and dormant code created the conditions.

title: Pentium FDIV: A Rare Arithmetic Error and a Public Trust Crisis
dek: The 1994 processor flaw became a case about numerical edge cases, disclosure and replacement policy.
event: A flaw in some Intel Pentium processors produced incorrect results for certain floating-point division operations. Public disclosure in 1994 turned a rare technical error into a debate about reliability and customer response.
mechanism: The article must explain the missing lookup-table entries and their numerical effect without exaggerating how often typical users would encounter the error.
system: The incident asks how a manufacturer decides whether a low-probability correctness defect is material, who receives replacement and how independent researchers challenge internal risk estimates.
memory: The faulty division examples are memorable; Intel's initial response and later replacement policy made the issue a broader case in technology trust.

title: Mariner 1: Guidance, Transcription and the Myth of a Missing Hyphen
dek: The 1962 launch failure became a software legend whose repeated shorthand needs careful correction.
event: The Mariner 1 spacecraft was destroyed shortly after launch in July 1962 when its launch vehicle deviated from the intended path. The failure involved guidance-signal handling and an error in the equations used by ground guidance.
mechanism: The article must distinguish hardware beacon problems, smoothing logic, handwritten notation and implemented code, using technical histories to test the missing-hyphen story.
system: Mariner 1 asks how mathematical notation moves through specification, transcription, programming and verification when several representations must mean the same thing.
memory: The missing hyphen survives because it is simple; the actual guidance chain is more instructive and less easily reduced to punctuation.

title: Hubble's Mirror: A Precise Shape Built From the Wrong Reference
dek: The telescope's original optical flaw showed how measurement equipment can make a wrong result look exact.
event: After Hubble Space Telescope entered orbit in 1990, images revealed spherical aberration in its primary mirror. Investigation traced the error to the optical test setup used during fabrication, while other test evidence had indicated a problem.
mechanism: The article must explain the null corrector, mirror figure and conflicting measurements without treating precision as accuracy.
system: Hubble asks how teams respond when one authoritative instrument disagrees with other tests and when schedule or organizational boundaries discourage resolving the discrepancy.
memory: The later repair mission creates a triumphant ending; the manufacturing investigation remains a powerful record of calibrated error and ignored contradiction.

source.title: Hubble Space Telescope flawed mirror overview

title: The Millennium Bridge: When Pedestrians Synchronized With the Structure
dek: London's new footbridge opened in 2000 and revealed a lateral vibration mechanism not adequately anticipated in design.
event: The London Millennium Footbridge developed unexpected lateral movement when large crowds crossed during its opening in June 2000. The bridge was closed and later fitted with damping systems.
mechanism: The article must explain lateral force, pedestrian adjustment and feedback without repeating the inaccurate idea that people simply marched in unison from the start.
system: The case asks how design standards capture interactions between people and flexible structures that emerge only at full scale and high occupancy.
memory: The nickname wobbly bridge makes the event comic; the engineering value lies in observing a new feedback mechanism and changing practice without structural collapse.

title: Citicorp Center: The Wind Load Recalculation and the Quiet Retrofit
dek: A design review after construction revealed vulnerability in a prominent tower and triggered an emergency strengthening program.
event: Questions raised after completion of New York's Citicorp Center led engineer William LeMessurier to re-examine wind loads and connection changes in the tower. A retrofit was organized while the building remained a major public landmark.
mechanism: The article must distinguish original design assumptions, quartering winds, welded versus bolted joints, tuned-mass-damper dependence and the actual safety margins found in later review.
system: The case asks how professional responsibility, disclosure, emergency planning and public communication operate when a serious design concern emerges after occupancy.
memory: The story is often told as a lone engineer's ethical triumph; archival disputes and the roles of other engineers, contractors and owners require a less heroic frame.
